text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Recent reports have revealed that Norway violates the United Nation's convention for children. Children under 18 years of age who apply for political asylum in Norway have no legal rights until they are granted residency permits.

- Svein Aaser, head of pharmaceuticals group Nycomed ASA, will propably receive a 100 percent pay rise when Nycomed merges with Britain's Amersham International Plc. Aaser earned two million crowns a year as head of Nycomed.
- An increasing number of Norwegian brokerage houses expect interest rates to rise in the next few months. The increase is mainly due to expectations of higher rates in Europe.

-Aage Korsvold, head of Storebrand ASA, says Norway's largest insurer will probably merge with a foreign company next time it seeks an alliance. An extraordinary meeting of Storebrand shareholders at the end of June turned down a proposed merger with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA.
- Norwegians have sharply increased investments on the Oslo bourse. Since January, 1996, private investments on the bourse have risen by 26 billion crowns to 61 billion crowns.

- Oil companies expect another year of record results. So far this year the average oil price has been $0.50 per barrel higher than last year and oil market players have a positive outlook for the next six months.
